name: clinical_v0_gate212_shoulder
rationale: Composed final-layer weights identify units 198 and 38 as positive readout paths that activate for high normalized values. In 128 calibration patients, their active cases remain underestimated after the original affine correction; almost all are measured variables rather than static/administrative channels. Increase only these two effective output coefficients by 1%, a fixed conservative expansion of the existing learned paths. Negative GELU-tail contributions change in the opposite direction, also consistent with the common positive offset in the low/middle range. No fitting, gradients, optimizer or test data. Exact median-draw activations of the edited model show unit 198 still underestimating in its positive intermediate range (median normalized errors -0.0128, -0.0327, -0.0492 in activation bins 0-0.5, 0.5-1, 1-2), across 93, 81, 96 calibration patients. Above 2 the median error reverses sign to +0.0223. Add a localized triangular correction in preactivation z198: k*(GELU(16*z)-4*GELU(16*(z-1.5))+3*GELU(16*(z-2)))/16, k=0.04*the current effective coefficient. It rises toward the strongest intermediate underestimation and switches off before the high tail. A single fixed 4% slope is used; no fitting or sweep. Reuse three existing neurons with negligible effective contributions. Unit 38 is unchanged because its remaining residual signs are inconsistent. The running benchmark candidate remains unchanged; no clinical test result informed this proposal. Compose the independent 1% sharpening of negative-only head unit 47, using its already specified weights unchanged. The local positive repair reduced mean confirmation MSE but cost MAE; unit 47 sharpening reduced MAE on both confirmation seeds but slightly cost MSE. They address intermediate underestimation and a common positive negative-tail contribution through disjoint neurons. No coefficient is refitted, searched or derived from test. Test their composition as a single new hypothesis, retaining it only if full forward evaluations support joint improvement. New calibration median-draw preactivations show unit 255 remains entirely negative. Its negative coefficient turns GELU's negative lobe into a positive output hump. For z in [-1.5,-1), residual median is +0.00673; for z in [-1,-0.5), it is -0.00197, each across 127 patients. Translate this hump by changing only incoming bias 255 by -0.01. This lowers its left-tail contribution and raises its contribution near zero, unlike uniform attenuation. The pattern is stronger on static/admin/time variables; physiological subgroup signs are mixed. This is one fixed hypothesis on an experimental parent, not a demonstrated causal correction. No gradients, training, parameter sweep or test residuals are used. V1 test scores have already been seen in the ongoing benchmark; any later test is a repeated benchmark assessment. A separate local hypothesis targets the near-zero shoulder of negative-coefficient unit212. In the unchanged V3 calibration512 diagnostic, z212 in [-0.5,0) occurs at456 scoring entries across211 patients. Both median and mean normalized residuals are positive overall and in the physiological subgroup; the association is mixed by variable and is not causal proof. Reuse nearly disconnected units4,133,144 to implement a smooth triangular subtraction: A*(GELU(64*(z+0.5))-2*GELU(64*(z+0.25))+GELU(64*z))/64, where A=-0.05*abs(effective_coefficient212). The ideal triangular response vanishes on both sides of the selected interval instead of extending a new constant correction above zero. GELU smoothing creates small boundary lobes; stored float32 weights are verified separately. Thresholds, midpoint, sharpness and5% coefficient fraction are fixed before candidate evaluation; none are fitted to residual amplitudes. This starts from V3 and includes neither V4's relative-tail program nor gate12 nor the rejected unit167 program. No training, gradients, optimizer, coefficient sweep, confirmation residuals or test residuals are used.
